ask: Announce our new Lisbon office on LinkedIn, X and Threads: it's our second office, eight of us start there in January, and we're hiring two engineers. Same news, but write it right for each one.

steps.why: Limits once for the networks named: X 280, Threads 500, LinkedIn 3,000. Each version is counted against its own network.
The three account ids. Any account marked for reconnecting is named before writing for it.

arguments.content: We've opened a second office, in Lisbon. Eight of us start there in January, and we're hiring two engineers.

linkedin.text:
We've opened our second office, in Lisbon.

Eight of us start there in January.

We're also hiring two engineers. Ask me anything about the team.

x.text: New office: Lisbon. Eight of us start in January, and we're hiring two engineers.

threads.text: We picked Lisbon for our second office. Eight of us start there in January. Anyone here worked from Lisbon? Tips welcome.

steps.why: The decision: one post, because the media, time and number of parts are the same and only the words differ; one yes covers all three. A fresh text per network in platform_specific, written separately with different first lines: LinkedIn gets room and an invitation, X one line, Threads a question. content stays as the fallback. The Threads topic goes in the same call; through platform_specific it needs no use_topic_tag. X carries text only: an X setting here would not be sent on a new post. Every fact is from the ask. Saved as a draft: no time, no action.
Read back: metadata.platformSpecific holds each network's text and the topic as Bolta stored them.

say: Saved to Acme as one draft for 3 networks. 1. LinkedIn: (full text) 2. X: (full text) 3. Threads: (full text), topic Startups. Nothing goes out yet. One yes covers all three. Schedule it?
never: Pasting the LinkedIn text into X and trimming it.
Showing only the main text: each network's own text is what goes out.
Using per-network text for TikTok, YouTube, Pinterest or WordPress: they ignore it.
Splitting into three posts when nothing differs but the words.
